# SIMULATED recruiting pipeline

Neither public dataset contains recruiting data, so time to hire is shown with a
**SIMULATED** pipeline generated by `src/simulate_hiring.py` (Python `random`, seed
`20261028`). Running the script again gives exactly the same files:

- `data/simulated/SIMULATED_requisitions.csv`, 300 requisitions
- `data/simulated/SIMULATED_candidates.csv`, 12,109 candidate applications

**Nothing in these files is a real measurement.** Any number computed from them
reflects the assumptions below.

## How it is tied to the IBM data

The only real input is the IBM file. Each requisition picks a department and job role
with a probability proportional to the number of IBM leavers (Attrition = Yes) in that
department and role, so roles that lose more people get more backfill requisitions. The
job level is the median job level of that role at IBM.

## Assumptions

| Assumption | Value |
|---|---|
| Requisitions | 300, opened uniformly between 1 Jan 2025 and 30 Jun 2026 |
| Snapshot date | 30 Sep 2026. Events after that date are removed (open requisitions, pending offers) |
| Applicants per requisition | Lognormal, mean by job level: L1 45, L2 32, L3 24, L4 16, L5 12 (minimum 3) |
| Application lag after opening | Exponential, mean 9 days |
| Applicant sources | LinkedIn 32%, Job board 25%, Careers site 20%, Employee referral 13%, Agency 10% |
| Screen pass rate | LinkedIn 30%, Job board 22%, Careers site 30%, Employee referral 55%, Agency 45% |
| Screen to first interview | 60% |
| First interview to final round | 40% |
| Offers | Made to finalists one at a time, in order of their final interview, until one accepts |
| Offer accept rate | LinkedIn 78%, Job board 74%, Careers site 80%, Employee referral 90%, Agency 70% |
| Days applied to screen / screen to interview / interview to final / final to offer / offer to decision | uniform 2-10 / 4-14 / 5-15 / 2-8 / 1-6 |
| Notice period (accept to start) | uniform 14-60 days |
| Requisitions cancelled without a hire | 6%, cancelled 20-90 days after opening |

Because delays do not depend on department or role, the simulated time to hire is
almost the same in every department. That is a property of the simulation, not a finding.
